theory.intro: Each straight-line segment of a distance–time graph is travelled at a constant speed, and that speed is the steepness of the segment. Read the distance the segment covers (its **rise**) and the time it takes (its **run**) straight off the axes, then divide. Steeper segments give larger speeds; a horizontal segment gives a speed of $0$.
facts: $\text{speed}=\dfrac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}}=\dfrac{\text{change in distance}}{\text{change in time}}$ for a straight segment.
Always check the scale on **both** axes before reading a value — one grid square is rarely one unit.
For a segment that does not start at the origin, subtract: use the distance **change** and the time **change**, not the end readings.
A segment sloping **down** is a return journey; its speed is the size of the change, written as a positive number.
If the time axis is in minutes, convert to hours before giving a speed in km/h: $20$ min $=\frac{1}{3}$ h.
steps: Read the two end points of the segment from the axes.
Find the change in distance and the change in time.
Divide the change in distance by the change in time.

development.solution_text:
$s_{1}=\frac{80-0}{1-0}$
$=80\text{ km/h}$
$s_{2}=\frac{200-80}{4-2}$
$=60\text{ km/h}$
$80-60=20$, so the train was $20$ km/h faster before the stop.

$s_{\text{Theo}}=\frac{50-0}{2-0}$
$=25\text{ km/h}$
$s_{\text{Rani}}=\frac{60}{4}$
$=15\text{ km/h}$
$25-15=10$, so Theo was riding $10$ km/h faster than Rani.

mastery.solution_text:
$s_{\text{before}}=\frac{50-0}{1-0}$
$=50\text{ km/h}$
$s_{\text{after}}=\frac{140-50}{4-2}$
$=\frac{90}{2}$
$=45\text{ km/h}$
$45<50$, so Marisol is wrong — she was $5$ km/h slower after the stop.

$s_{\text{Amara}}=\frac{72-36}{2-0}$
$=\frac{36}{2}$
$=18\text{ km/h}$
$s_{\text{Kwame}}=\frac{72-24}{2-0}$
$=\frac{48}{2}$
$=24\text{ km/h}$
$24-18=6$, so Kwame was riding $6$ km/h faster.
